nodes.description: Internal function createProxy(address target, bytes32 salt) that builds minimal-proxy bytecode and deploys it deterministically with create2.
Public function deployModule(address masterCopy, bytes memory initializer, uint256 saltNonce) that deploys a proxy and immediately performs a low-level call with attacker-supplied initializer data.
Implicit caller of the public deployModule entrypoint; anyone can invoke deployment and supply the initializer payload.
Inline assembly create2(0, add(deployment,0x20), mload(deployment), salt) executing raw runtime bytecode with a caller-controlled salt and target address.
Unchecked low-level proxy.call(initializer) sending arbitrary calldata to a freshly created proxy contract before state finalization; external code executes mid-transaction.
Parameter target of createProxy: master copy address embedded into the proxy bytecode.
Parameter salt of createProxy: user-influenced 32-byte value passed to create2.
Parameter masterCopy of deployModule: implementation address used as the proxy target.
Parameter initializer of deployModule: arbitrary external calldata forwarded to the proxy.
Parameter saltNonce of deployModule: nonce hashed with the initializer to derive the create2 salt.
Local variable result of createProxy: address returned by the create2 deployment.
Local variable deployment of createProxy: assembled minimal-proxy creation bytecode.
Local variable proxy of deployModule: address of the newly created proxy contract.
Local variable success of deployModule: boolean returned by the low-level initializer call.

edges.reason: msg.sender can invoke the public deployModule entrypoint with arbitrary masterCopy, initializer and saltNonce.
deployModule calls the internal createProxy helper to deploy the proxy.
deployModule executes a raw external call to the freshly created proxy while the transaction is still in progress, exposing the deployment flow to reentrancy.
The proxy's initializer execution can call back into deployModule (or other factory logic) before the outer call finishes, enabling reentrant deployment.
target parameter flows into createProxy's zero-address check and into the assembled proxy bytecode.
target is embedded via abi.encodePacked into the deployment bytecode consumed by the create2 assembly.
salt parameter is used by createProxy to make the deployment address deterministic.
salt flows directly into the create2 assembly as the salt operand.
masterCopy parameter is used by deployModule as the implementation target of the proxy.
masterCopy is forwarded from deployModule into createProxy as the target argument.
initializer parameter is hashed for the salt and later executed against the proxy.
saltNonce parameter is hashed with the initializer to derive the create2 salt.
Caller-controlled initializer bytes are used as the calldata of the low-level proxy.call, letting an attacker choose what external code runs.
The proxy address produced by createProxy is the callee of the low-level call, so the external invocation target is derived from the create2 deployment.
The assembled deployment bytecode is read from memory inside the create2 assembly.
The address returned by create2 is stored into the result return variable.
The result returned by createProxy is assigned to the proxy variable in deployModule.
The boolean returned by the low-level call populates the success variable used in the require.
